### Prerequisites

We suggest you first read the texts about navigating the menus and about the menu options.

### Introduction

While reading History Tracers, you will notice that some words, names, and numbers are clickable links. These links connect the text to the sources that support it. This guide explains how to click on them and where the information appears.

### Links in the text A link is a word or phrase shown in a different color and, usually, underlined. When you move the pointer over it, the cursor becomes a hand. Click on the link to open its source on the right side of the screen, under the heading of the corresponding category. The example below is a reference: NOAA (2024). What is longitude?. Click on it and look at the *References* heading on the right.

### Conclusion

With these four categories you can always find the origin of what you are reading. Click on the links in any text and follow the sources on the right side of the screen.
